decision_reason: UNICEF's public-international investment in Convexity and official evidence of CHATS use are specific and strong, but the assigned link is an organization root rather than a mapped application source. The current CHATS suite spans multiple repositories; the legacy CHATS repository is Sempo-branded GPL code, the newer apps have separate AGPL grants, and the chats-donor repository exposes no grant. The exact production-source boundary and license coverage for the full product remain unresolved, so this is held rather than published.

government_provenance.note: The UNICEF Office of Innovation states that its Venture Fund and Crypto Fund selected Convexity Technologies (Nigeria) for the Giga blockchain cohort and would provide up to $100,000 in equity-free investment. UNICEF's 2023 cohort update ties the funded Convexity team to CHATS specifically. This is documented public-international sponsorship, not sovereign-state authorship; Convexity remains the private developer.

public_source.note: The public organization exposes source repositories for the CHATS system, including chats-api, chats-admin, chats-ngo, chats-blockchain, chats-vendor, chats-field, chats-beneficiary, chats-kyc, and chats-donor. The DPG record points to the organization root, not a canonical deployment manifest; the separate product-to-repository boundary is therefore recorded as unresolved under licensing.

eligible_license.note: The newer service/app repositories chats-api, chats-admin, chats-ngo, chats-blockchain, chats-vendor, chats-beneficiary, and chats-kyc each expose GNU AGPLv3 text; chats-field explicitly says AGPL-3.0-or-later. The older https://github.com/ConvexityTeam/CHATS/blob/master/LICENSE is GPLv3, while its README still describes Sempo rather than the current CHATS product. No license file or clear grant was found in the chats-donor repository. Until the production component list and rights for every material component are reconciled, the DPG's single AGPL label cannot be applied to the full suite.

primary_evidence.note: UNICEF's 2023 first-party cohort update says the CHATS MVP was beta-tested for humanitarian cash/voucher projects, names humanitarian organizations using it, and reports more than 10,000 beneficiaries. UNICEF's 2023-24 Venture Fund annual report later attributes 13,613 beneficiaries across three humanitarian projects to Convexity's CHATS; the current product site remains live at https://chats.cash/. These sources establish substantive product use, though not current source-code parity.

product_identity: CHATS, Convexity Technologies' blockchain-based humanitarian cash-and-voucher assistance platform, comprising donor/NGO dashboards, beneficiary and field/vendor apps, KYC and transaction services
agency: UNICEF Venture Fund and UNICEF Crypto Fund (public-international investment through the Giga blockchain cohort); Convexity Technologies Ltd. is the private product developer
geography: Nigeria-origin product with humanitarian deployments across multiple countries
license: Mixed and unresolved at product level: AGPLv3 grants across most newer app/service repositories, AGPL-3.0-or-later for chats-field, GPLv3 for the Sempo-branded legacy CHATS repository, and no clear grant found for chats-donor
family_note: The assigned GitHub URL is an organization, not one source repository. This review treats CHATS as one multi-application product only; the old Sempo-branded CHATS repository is not assumed to be the canonical source of the newer named platform. No catalog match was found.
status_note: The earliest located grant-bearing source for the current named app suite is a 2023 license-bearing component commit; the 2019 GPL grant belongs to a repository whose README identifies Sempo, not the current CHATS suite. UNICEF's first-party reports establish funded deployment/use and the public product site is current, but no authoritative deployment-to-repository map was located. Review the current component boundary and all grants before reconsidering publishability.

decision_reason: The whole core CARE web application is now verified as a two-repository family: the MIT-licensed backend and the separate MIT-licensed care_fe frontend. Their first public grant-bearing commits are March 17 and April 8, 2020 respectively; both canonical repos remain active, and 10BedICU's public organization maintains current forks of both while its current product page identifies CARE as the deployed EMR. AICTE/GDC public support is attributed only to named oxygen-monitoring and critical-care modules, not all CARE code.

government_provenance.note: Government of India's DARPG proceedings describe the CoronaSafe system operating Kerala COVID warrooms and the AICTE/Pupilfirst Global Digital Corps program that built software for National Health Mission warrooms during the oxygen crisis. CARE's own product requirements at https://docs.coronasafe.network/coronasafe-care-documentation specifically say the AICTE-supported fellowship graduates built its real-time oxygen-monitoring and critical-care modules. This establishes product-specific public-agency-supported development, not merely later government use; ACT grants were philanthropic, and the government contribution is attributed specifically to AICTE.

public_source.note: The assigned coronasafe/care URL redirects to canonical ohcnetwork/care. The complete core web app also requires the separate public ohcnetwork/care_fe frontend, whose README links the backend documentation and provides local frontend setup/staging details. GitHub's repository API identifies https://api.github.com/repos/10bedicu/care as a fork whose parent is ohcnetwork/care, and https://api.github.com/repos/10bedicu/care_fe as a fork whose parent is ohcnetwork/care_fe; both were pushed 2026-09-28. This directly maps the current 10BedICU source family to both canonical repos. Optional plugins and deployment infrastructure are outside this core-app scope.

eligible_license.note: I inspected the root grants separately: MIT applies to first-party backend code in ohcnetwork/care, and MIT applies to first-party web-frontend code in ohcnetwork/care_fe (https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/blob/develop/LICENSE). The backend's first LICENSE-bearing source commit is 2020-03-17; the frontend's is 2020-04-08. These separate grants do not cover optional plug-in repositories, third-party dependencies, or the wider TeleICU/equipment infrastructure.

primary_evidence.note: 10BedICU's current CARE platform page describes CARE as its deployed EMR and documents the hospital-facing patient-management platform and training. GitHub's direct repository API records show https://api.github.com/repos/10bedicu/care is a current fork of ohcnetwork/care and https://api.github.com/repos/10bedicu/care_fe is a current fork of ohcnetwork/care_fe (both pushed 2026-09-28), explicitly mapping the deployed CARE source family to the two canonical repos rather than inferring correspondence from matching names. Meghalaya's government launch record and the 10BedICU program page establish state-government deployment/use; this is not used as proof of authorship.

product_identity: CARE core EMR web application: the Coronasafe-origin healthcare patient-management and critical-care platform comprising the CARE backend/API plus the separate care_fe web interface; optional plugins and TeleICU infrastructure are excluded
agency: All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), Government of India, supported the GDC fellowship whose fellows built CARE modules; current product stewardship is with Open Healthcare Network/eGovernments Foundation, with 10BedICU state-government deployments
geography: India; originated in Kerala and currently deployed through public-private state programs across multiple states
license: MIT for first-party backend source in ohcnetwork/care and separately MIT for first-party web frontend source in ohcnetwork/care_fe; dependencies and optional plugins remain separately licensed
family_note: The assigned coronasafe/care path redirects to canonical ohcnetwork/care; the deployed core application is explicitly mapped to the two-repository family by current 10BedICU forks whose GitHub API parent fields point to ohcnetwork/care and ohcnetwork/care_fe. Each repo has its own root MIT grant: backend grant/source commit 2020-03-17 (https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care/commit/9be04171f9a31f82ce038d8c7ed2be2fc9b82998), frontend grant commit 2020-04-08 (https://github.com/ohcnetwork/care_fe/commit/f86d0ee7bb55b5283b939b48503fd51562554cc6). This entry is only the core backend+web-frontend application, not optional ABDM/HMIS/other plugs, TeleICU network infrastructure, or equipment. No catalog match was found.
status_note: The core app's first licensed source is dated 2020-03-17 in the backend; the separate frontend's MIT grant was committed 2020-04-08. Both canonical repos show current 2026 activity. 10BedICU's public organization has active forks whose GitHub parent fields point to ohcnetwork/care and ohcnetwork/care_fe; its current product page identifies CARE as its operating EMR. CARE originated with Coronasafe/OHC; AICTE-supported GDC fellows built specifically named oxygen-monitoring and critical-care modules, and this government relationship is not attributed to every repository file.

decision_reason: Corosync is a mature, actively maintained open-source cluster engine with a precise BSD grant and independent distribution, but the project history identifies it as a community derivative of OpenAIS developed by private-sector contributors, not a government-created, commissioned, funded, or stewarded product. Its appearance in France's SILL is a discovery/catalog lead and does not establish public provenance.

government_provenance.note: The project's own history says Corosync was created as a derivative of OpenAIS to form a distinct cluster-infrastructure community; the repository's copyright history identifies MontaVista and Red Hat contributors. No public agency authorship, funding, commissioning, or stewardship for this exact product was found. The assigned French SILL listing is not provenance evidence.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository exposes Corosync's complete cluster-engine source, build/install material, documentation, and current source history without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root license explicitly applies the three-condition BSD grant to every file in the source distribution except git-version-gen and gitlog-to-changelog; those two release-process helpers are GPLv3-or-later and are not part of the generated binary. The scoped BSD-3-Clause grant covers the cluster-engine product code.

primary_evidence.note: Fedora's official package page distributes Corosync as a current cluster-engine package (3.1.10 in the current package metadata) with Fedora build and source links. This is evidence of independent distribution and product maturity, not evidence of government sponsorship or government deployment.

product_identity: Corosync Cluster Engine, the OpenAIS-derived cluster messaging, membership, quorum, and service-infrastructure engine
agency: No government agency identified; early source history names MontaVista Software and Red Hat contributors, followed by the Corosync developer community
geography: International open-source infrastructure project; no government sponsor geography established
license: BSD-3-Clause for the Corosync product files; GPL-3.0-or-later for two release-process helper scripts only
family_note: Review covers the Corosync Cluster Engine source, not a vendor's HA distribution or any government's use of it. The source history contains earlier OpenAIS code; 2008 is the Corosync product's founding/public project year, not the inherited OpenAIS code's earlier license date. No catalog match was found.
status_note: The 2008 Ottawa Linux Symposium paper by project developers describes Corosync as an open-source cluster engine and says it was founded in January 2008; current repository activity reached 2026-09-07. Fedora independently packages the engine. The SILL entry is retained only as the assigned lead and did not affect the provenance decision.

decision_reason: Creative Commons Legal Tools is an active public-interest application maintained by Creative Commons, an independent nonprofit, but no government agency authorship, commissioning, funding, or stewardship for this exact application was established. The DPG profile's statement that government institutions use Creative Commons tools is self-reported and does not demonstrate a government's relationship to this source repository.

government_provenance.note: Creative Commons identifies itself as an independent nonprofit organization, and the application README says it is the CC team's tool for managing Creative Commons licenses and public-domain tools. No government agency relationship for this software was found. Use of Creative Commons licenses by public institutions would not prove government origin of this application.

public_source.note: The application repository is public, contains the application source and developer setup, and explicitly links its companion cc-legal-tools-data repository from which it consumes and generates legal-tool data.

eligible_license.note: The assigned application-code repository grants MIT to its first-party software. The companion data repository is a separate content scope with CC0/public-domain and CC-BY-4.0 material as documented in the DPG record; those content grants are not substituted for the app's code license or assumed to relicense dependencies.

primary_evidence.note: The Creative Commons chooser is publicly accessible and the application documentation describes a mature tool managing hundreds of license and public-domain instruments. The DPG record claims broad government/ministerial adoption but labels adopter information self-reported; I found no independent primary source documenting a specific government's use of this application or government distribution of this code. Use of CC legal licenses is not evidence of use of this distinct software.

product_identity: Creative Commons Legal Tools Application, the Ruby application that manages and generates Creative Commons license and public-domain deeds; the legal-tool content is a separate companion data repository
agency: No government agency identified; developed and maintained by Creative Commons, an independent nonprofit
geography: Global, with no government sponsor geography established
license: MIT for the assigned application code; companion legal-tool data has separate CC0/CC-BY content grants, and dependencies are separately licensed
family_note: The application repository is only the executable/data-management part of a two-repository legal-tools suite; this review does not treat CC's license texts or public-domain instruments as source code. The DPG's CC-BY metadata concerns content and does not replace the app repository's MIT grant. No catalog match was found.
status_note: The first root MIT-license commit was 2020-06-03; the assigned repository remains active, with source changes through 2026-09-23. Its current Creative Commons-hosted chooser establishes public operation, but the government's use of Creative Commons licensing standards is not transferred to this app and no exact public-sector application deployment was independently documented.

decision_reason: CREDEBL is a real, actively maintained decentralized-identity platform used as a protocol layer in Bhutan's government National Digital Identity, but the project's first-party sources identify AYANWORKS as its private developer and product owner. Neither deployment of the vendor's platform nor its Digital Public Goods registration establishes government authorship, commissioning, funding, or stewardship of the product source.

government_provenance.note: CREDEBL's own site says the platform was created from AYANWORKS's private team's experience deploying prior identity solutions; the Linux Foundation Decentralized Trust source identifies it as developed and maintained by AYANWORKS. Bhutan's NDI uses CREDEBL as a protocol layer, but that is third-party government use, not proof that the Government of Bhutan funded or created this general product.

public_source.note: The assigned organization is public and links the platform, Studio UI, agent controller, installation tooling, mobile SDK, and reference wallet repositories. The core code is accessible without credentials; the DPG source record points to this organization-level index rather than a single repository.

eligible_license.note: First-party LICENSE files in the core platform, Studio, agent-controller, install, mobile-sdk, platform-admin, webauthn-server, and reference mobile-wallet repositories grant Apache-2.0 to their respective repository code. This is a multi-repository scope, not a grant to every repository or upstream dependency in the AYANWORKS account.

primary_evidence.note: The Royal Government of Bhutan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs reports 2026 integration of the Bhutan NDI wallet/eKYC with the national passport system. CREDEBL's own current technology page says it is the NDI initiative's protocol layer. Together these primary sources verify an operational government use of this exact third-party platform, but not public authorship or funding.

product_identity: CREDEBL, AYANWORKS's multi-repository self-sovereign/decentralized identity and verifiable-credential platform, including the platform service, Studio UI, agent controller, installation tools, SDK, and reference wallet
agency: No government creator or source sponsor identified; private product owner/developer AYANWORKS; Royal Government of Bhutan is a documented downstream user of CREDEBL within NDI
geography: Developed by AYANWORKS in India; deployed as the protocol layer for Bhutan's national digital identity
license: Apache-2.0 for the identified first-party CREDEBL core repositories, with per-repository scopes; dependencies and any non-core or upstream code remain separately licensed
family_note: The assigned URL is an organization page. The reviewed product is the identified CREDEBL suite, not every AYANWORKS repository; core components and license scopes are named separately. Government NDI deployment is treated as third-party use only. No catalog match was found.
status_note: The earliest inspected first-party CREDEBL UI source with an Apache grant dates from 2023-06-21; the core platform repository began in 2023-08. The platform source remains active, with code updates in September 2026, and current product/docs pages link to the platform. Current Bhutan government use is corroborated by the Royal Government's 2026 NDI service announcement plus CREDEBL's explicit implementation mapping. No exact catalog match was found.
